segunSemaforo.verde: Good time: go out at the indicated time and shoot several times, because the clouds can move.
segunSemaforo.ambar: It can turn out well if there are gaps between the clouds. Wait and shoot when the moon peeks out.
segunSemaforo.rojo: Today the sensible thing is not to go out. If you go, try the clouds lit by the moon.

variantes.nota: Without a telephoto lens the moon will come out small. It works better included in a landscape, with buildings or trees.

pasos.empiezo: Tap the moon on the screen.
pasos.defiendo: When you tap the moon the phone measures the light on it and not on the dark sky, which would turn it into a white blob.
pasos.controlo: Tap the moon (lock exposure and focus)

pasos.empiezo: Lower the brightness until the moon's markings show.
pasos.defiendo: The moon is very bright; lowering the brightness lets you make out the craters.

pasos.empiezo: Rest the phone and use the 2-second timer.
pasos.defiendo: At night the phone takes longer to shoot; supported and with the timer it comes out sharp.

pasos.empiezo: Turn the mode dial to M.
pasos.defiendo: In [[modo-m|M]] you control everything. On auto the camera overexposes the moon, because it is surrounded by dark sky.
f/8: the [[apertura|aperture]] that gives the most sharpness on most lenses.
The moon gives off a lot of light: you don't need a high [[iso|ISO]].

pasos.empiezo: Set the shutter speed between 1/250 and 1/500 seconds.
pasos.defiendo: With that [[velocidad|shutter speed]] the moon comes out sharp even as it moves across the sky.

pasos.empiezo: Switch the focus to manual, zoom in on the moon on the screen and turn the ring until the edges look sharp.
pasos.defiendo: [[enfoque-manual|Manual focus]] works better than autofocus with an object so far away and so bright.
The [[disparador|timer]] keeps your finger from moving the camera.

variantes.nota: With a telephoto lens any shake shows a lot. Look for a firm support and shoot several times: some will come out sharp.

pasos.defiendo: In [[modo-tv|{Tv}]] you choose the shutter speed, which is what matters without a tripod.

pasos.empiezo: Set the shutter speed to 1/500 seconds.
pasos.defiendo: A fast [[velocidad|shutter speed]] makes up for hand shake with the telephoto lens.

pasos.empiezo: Lower the exposure compensation to -2 (the button with +/-).
pasos.defiendo: [[compensacion|-2]]: it darkens a little so the brightest parts don't blow out.

pasos.empiezo: Leave the ISO on auto and set a limit of 3200 in the menu.
pasos.defiendo: Auto [[iso|ISO]] keeps the shutter speed fast; the limit holds back the grain.

pasos.empiezo: Rest the camera or the lens against a wall, a post or a railing.
pasos.defiendo: The steadier it is, the sharper it will come out.

variantes.nota: With the normal lens (for example 18-55) the moon will be a small dot. It works better included in a landscape.

pasos.defiendo: Turn the mode dial to [[modo-av|{Av}]]: you choose the aperture and the camera works out the rest.

pasos.empiezo: Raise the f-number to f/8. Without a tripod, use the lowest f-number you have.
pasos.defiendo: f/8 gives good sharpness; without a tripod it's best to open up all the way to be able to use a large [[apertura|aperture]] and a fast shutter speed.
pasos.controlo: f/8 (without a tripod, the widest aperture)

pasos.empiezo: Lower the exposure compensation to -2 (the button with +/-).
pasos.defiendo: [[compensacion|-2]]: it darkens a little so the brightest parts don't blow out.

pasos.empiezo: With a tripod, ISO 100. Without a tripod, auto ISO with a limit of 3200.
pasos.defiendo: With a tripod the [[iso|ISO]] can be low; without one, auto keeps the shutter speed up and the limit holds back the grain.

pasos.empiezo: With a tripod, turn on the 2-second timer. Without one, rest the camera on something firm.
pasos.defiendo: The [[disparador|timer]] or a firm support keeps the photo from coming out blurred.
